objective: Reduce the number of tracked files a planning run needs to read.
summary: The repository includes tools for listing, reading, and searching files, but the current implementation reads all tracked files during planning. The goal is to optimize this by reducing the number of files read, potentially by prioritizing or caching frequently accessed files. The files `src/plan.js`, `src/repository.js`, and `src/graph.js` handle the planning and file operations, but there's no evidence of optimization for file access yet.

nodes.title: Identify frequently accessed files during planning
nodes.reason: To reduce the number of files read, we need to know which files are accessed most often during planning. This will help prioritize or cache them.
evidence: src/plan.js:46-47 — The planning process uses `repositoryTools` to investigate files.
src/repository.js:36-98 — The `repositoryTools` function handles file operations but doesn't track access patterns.

nodes.title: Implement a caching mechanism for frequently accessed files
nodes.reason: Caching frequently accessed files can reduce the number of file reads during planning, improving efficiency.
evidence: src/repository.js:36-98 — The `repositoryTools` function currently reads files on demand without caching.
src/plan.js:46-47 — The planning process relies on direct file reads.

nodes.title: Optimize the file search process
nodes.reason: The current search process scans all files, which can be inefficient. Optimizing it to skip or prioritize certain files can reduce overhead.
evidence: src/repository.js:76-90 — The `search` function scans all files linearly.
src/plan.js:46-47 — The planning process uses the search function for evidence gathering.
